sentences.text:
17.11.2023 Order No. (Through hybrid mode)
01.
1.

This is an application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with Korei P.S. Case No.269 of 2023 corresponding to C.T. Case No.1110 of 2023, pending in the file of the learned J.M.F.C., Jajpur Road under Sections 376 (2) (n)/506 of IPC.
2.

The prayer for bail of the petitioner had been rejected by order dated 06.10.2023 passed by the learned Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Jajpur Road in BLAPL No.318 of 2023 after referring to the FIR, statement of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. observing that the victim is consistent in her version regarding the allegation of rape and that investigation of the case was in progress.

entities.text: Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Jajpur Road
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The prosecution allegation in brief is that about eight months back when the victim had gone to graze her goats, the petitioner had kept sexual relations with her using force and thereafter when she had gone to the house of the uncle of the petitioner to watch T.V., the petitioner threatened her and continued to have physical relations with her, as a result of which she became pregnant, out of shame, she could not inform her parents as her mother is mentally challenged.
When she felt unwell, her father took her to the hospital for treatment and thereafter they learnt that she was pregnant..
4. Mr. Arijeet Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that it is a case of consent.
As the petitioner refused to marry the victim, she had lodged the FIR against him making false allegations that the petitioner had kept physical relations with her forcibly.

sentences.text: 1 5. Mr.D.K.Mishra, learned Addl.

Government Advocate opposes the prayer for bail stating that a case of rape is squarely made out against the petitioner as in the FIR the victim has stated that the petitioner had kept physical relationship with her using force and even though she has become pregnant, he refused to marry her.
He further submits that the investigation is in progress.

6. Considering the nature of allegations against the petitioner, her age and the age of the petitioner and the fact that investigation is in progress, I am not inclined to release the petitioner on bail at this stage and dismiss the BLAPL.
7. It is open to the petitioner to move for bail afresh after completion of investigation, if so advised.
8. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
